card: This pull request implements Windows support for Bitcoin Core's IPC subsystem and pulls in corresponding upstream libmultiprocess subtree updates. It replaces Unix-specific process spawning and socket communication with Windows named pipes, WSADuplicateSocket, and overlapped I/O, while fixing the Windows wrapper executable to properly await child processes. The changes also consolidate Windows PE resource generation across binaries into CMake and enable IPC test coverage on Windows. This work is a prerequisite for running multiprocess Bitcoin on Windows (#28722) and resolves libmultiprocess issues #53 and #114.
changed_since_previous: Incorporated subsequent upstream libmultiprocess commits, added MSVC fixes (including `/bigobj` for `mptest` and compiler warning suppressions), updated vcpkg configurations for CI fuzz builds, and refined Windows socket and errno handling.
evidence: Resolves libmultiprocess issues #53 and #114 according to the PR description
Part of the broader process separation project (tracking issue #28722)
problem: Bitcoin Core's IPC features and multiprocess mode cannot build or run on Windows because libmultiprocess and internal process-spawning helpers rely on POSIX APIs (such as `fork`, `execvp`, and Unix domain sockets), preventing Windows testing and deployment of multiprocess binaries.

risk.why: Modifies Windows process execution logic and replaces the manifest and resource generation mechanism for all Windows release binaries.

scope_notes: Contains a major `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree update squashed alongside Core modifications, and temporarily disables the subtree linter check (`test/lint/test_runner/src/util.rs`). It also replaces all static Windows `.rc` resource files for executables with a dynamic CMake generator (`add_windows_exe_resources`).
summary: This pull request adds Windows support for Bitcoin Core's IPC subsystem and updates the libmultiprocess subtree. It replaces POSIX-only process spawning and socket primitives with Windows equivalents (named pipes, WSADuplicateSocket, overlapped I/O, and `_spawnvp`/`_cwait` process tracking), consolidates Windows executable manifest and resource handling into a CMake helper, and enables IPC targets across MinGW, MSVC, and CI environments.
